answers.answer: Deal 4 Player cards to each player with 2 players, 3 each with 3 players, and 2 each with 4 players. Remove the Epidemic cards before shuffling and dealing; pawns start in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: Deal Player cards; Deal roles.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Reveal 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching-color cubes in each named city; reveal 3 more and place 2 in each; reveal 3 more and place 1 in each. Put all 9 revealed cards on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.

Use 4 Epidemic cards for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, then stack them with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: Prepare the Player Deck.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; actions may be repeated and you may stop early. Cards discarded to pay action costs go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together (resolve Epidemics first, then get down to the 7-card limit), then Infect Cities. After all three phases, play passes to the left.

Drive/Ferry moves to a city connected by a white line and costs no card. Direct Flight discards the City card for the destination. Charter Flight discards the City card matching the city you are in to move anywhere. Shuttle Flight moves from a city with a research station to any other city with a research station and costs no card. White lines going off one board edge wrap to the other edge.
answers.evidence: Actions: Movement Actions; Special Rules & Edge Cases: Board wrapping.

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it there. If all six are built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than six, set the extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Actions: Build a Research Station; Special Rules & Edge Cases: Research station limit and extras.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen cured color from the city; it does not also clear another color. Treat each different color with a separate action. The uncured color is treated one cube at a time, also with a separate action per cube. Removed cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Actions: Treat Disease; Cure Procedure; Eradication.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city's color need not match. Existing cubes remain on the board; if no cubes of that color are on the board when the cure is discovered, eradicate it immediately and flip the marker.
answers.evidence: Actions: Discover a Cure; Cure Procedure.

answers.answer: Normally, give or take the City card matching the city where both players are. Both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.

When sharing knowledge, the Researcher may give any City card, rather than only the matching-city card, to a player in the same city. This transfer from the Researcher's hand may happen on either player's turn. The exception does not let another player give an arbitrary nonmatching card to the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Roles: Researcher; Special Rules & Edge Cases: Researcher exception.

answers.answer: After actions, draw the top 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and the players lose. Discards are not reshuffled.

Resolve the Epidemic in order: Increase the Infection Rate marker by one space; Infect by drawing the bottom Infection card. For a non-eradicated disease, place 3 cubes in its city, but with two already there add only one to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs. Resolve the outbreak, then discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify by reshuffling only the Infection Discard Pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the resolved Epidemic card from the game; do not draw a replacement.
After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards per turn, respectively.

Resolve all three steps of the first Epidemic, then all three steps of the second; Events may be played between the two. After resolving all Epidemics drawn, enforce the 7-card hand limit. The summary says Events cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card.

Flip Infection cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For each named city, place 1 matching-color cube unless that disease is eradicated; if the city already has 3 of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. A cured but not eradicated disease can still infect. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.

The first outbreak resolves by advancing the Outbreaks marker and spreading one cube to every connected city. If a connected city already has 3 of that color, a chain outbreak occurs there after the current outbreak resolves, advancing the marker again and spreading from that city. Do not add cubes to cities that already had an outbreak during this Infection card, so spread does not return into the first city if it already outbreaked. Each color can have up to 3 cubes in a city; different colors have separate caps.

No. Once the Infection card has been drawn, it cannot be interrupted with Airlift before resolving the outbreak; Events cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card. Airlift may be played after that card resolves and before the next Infection card is drawn. Any player may play it, and the player who plays it chooses its use; it moves any one pawn to any city (get permission for another player's pawn). It costs no action, and the Event is discarded to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards; Actions (Events are not actions); Infecting Cities.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes one Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. Capacity is one, and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.

As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn (with its owner's permission) to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own. Direct/Charter Flight discards come from the Dispatcher's hand; the Charter card matches the moved pawn's departure city. The Dispatcher cannot direct another pawn to Treat Disease or take another nonmovement action, and cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.

Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. They lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (the 8th outbreak), if they cannot place the required disease cubes because a color's supply is exhausted (during an epidemic, outbreak, or infection), or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after their actions because fewer than 2 remain.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Victory and Defeat; Drawing Player Cards.
